summary.text: 里 is an old graph analyzed as a field (田) over earth (土), representing a habitable place or settlement. It also came to write a distance measure; the timing and connection between those meanings are not established. In one reported bronze inscription, it writes the separate word 裏, “lining,” probably by sound, though the old referent’s name and pronunciation are not known here.

formation.text: Semantic compound: 田 (“field”) and 土 (“earth”) combine in the traditional analysis to represent a place where people live. This explains the graph as a source interpretation, not a proven account of the precise original referent. The selected Western Zhou bronze-style image is a modern redraw illustrating that analysis; the inscription itself was not independently examined.

components.text: 田 is the field element in the reported analysis of 里. The dictionary reports strokes in 田 and 土 running together in some bronze forms; this account does not establish a separate earlier form for 田 within the graph.

土 is the earth element in the reported analysis of 里. The dictionary reports that its dot was extended into a short stroke in later forms underlying seal script; this is a graphic change within the graph.

history.text: The graph is reported in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions. Later reported bronze forms show strokes in 田 and 土 running together, with a dot in 土 extended into a short stroke in forms underlying seal script. These details come from a dictionary’s account; the cited artifacts and glyphs were not independently inspected. The supplied bronze-style illustration is a modern vector redraw, not an artifact image.

A reported bronze inscription uses the whole graph 里 to write 裏 in a phrase about a garment lining. This is a proposed sound-based borrowing: the sign 里 was reused for a different word because the words may have sounded alike or similarly. The old referent’s name and pronunciation are not established here, so the sound match remains qualified. This whole-graph use does not make 里 a component of itself.

The account also reports 里 in early uses for a settlement-related title and a distance measure, and later manuscript uses for settlements, distance, and 理. The dossier does not establish the first emergence of these senses or a semantic chain connecting them.

uncertainties.text: The analysis of 田 plus 土 as a habitable place is supported as a traditional and dictionary interpretation, but does not prove the graph’s exact original referent. Proposals linking the village word to Proto-Sino-Tibetan forms or to 理 are not verified by the research documented here.

The earliest reported graph attestation is Western Zhou bronze, but it does not establish the earliest pronunciation or the first occurrence of each word sense. The artifacts and primary editions cited in the dictionary summary were not independently inspected.

The reported distance-measure and general interior senses lack a securely established first occurrence or semantic connection to the settlement sense. The sound relation between 里 and 裏 is supported as 裏’s phonetic analysis, but does not identify the original referent or earliest pronunciation of 里.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions (earliest reported graph attestation; exact first sense occurrence unresolved)
senses.text: The traditional account glosses 里 as habitation, and the dictionary reports a Western Zhou bronze use for a settlement-related title. This supports an early settlement sense, though the graph’s precise original referent remains interpretive.

senses.period: attested in bronze inscriptions; first emergence unresolved
senses.text: A bronze use for a distance measure is reported. This establishes an attestation, not when the sense began or how it relates to settlement.

senses.gloss: inside or interior, in the use associated with 裏/裡
senses.text: 里 is reported in one bronze inscription writing 裏 in a garment-lining phrase. That is evidence for use of the graph to write another word, not proof that “inside” developed semantically from 里’s settlement meaning. In later usage the interior sense is associated with 裏/裡.

senses.period: attested in historical uses; first emergence unresolved
senses.text: Village and neighborhood are recorded senses, and settlement uses are reported in early sources. The evidence here does not establish a dated development from habitation to village or neighborhood.

developments.text: In a reported bronze inscription, 里 writes 裏 in a garment-lining phrase. The proposed mechanism is reuse of the written sign for a different word because their pronunciations were similar; the old referent’s name and pronunciation are not established here. This is graph borrowing, not a meaning shift from settlement to lining.

limitations.text: The reported settlement, distance, and interior uses do not establish the first occurrence of each sense or a semantic chain among them. The interior example is a graph used to write 裏; it does not show that 里’s settlement meaning changed into “lining” or “inside.”

The phonetic analysis of 里 within 裏 does not establish the earliest pronunciation or original referent of 里. The reported borrowing of the whole graph for 裏 therefore has a proposed, qualified sound mechanism rather than a demonstrated sound comparison for the original referent.

overview.text: 里 combines a field and earth in an old interpretation for a habitable place or settlement. It also writes a distance measure. In one reported inscription it writes 裏, “lining,” probably because the words sounded alike, though the old name and sound are not established here.

components.text: 田 depicts a field, contributing the field element in the traditional explanation of the settlement graph.
土 depicts earth, contributing the earth element in that explanation.

takeaway.text: The bronze use of 里 for 裏 is a proposed sound-based borrowing, not evidence that “lining” developed from the settlement meaning.

relationships.text: In the reported analysis of 里 as 田 plus 土, 田 depicts a field and contributes that depicted element to the habitable-place interpretation.
In the reported analysis of 里 as 田 plus 土, 土 depicts earth and contributes that depicted element to the habitable-place interpretation.

里 is analyzed as the phonetic element in 裏. Both characters have current readings displayed as Mandarin lǐ and reported Middle Chinese category 來開三之上. That comparison supports the phonetic analysis within 裏; it does not establish the old referent or earliest pronunciation of 里. Japanese on-reading ri is also reported for both, but it is not evidence for the Chinese historical origin.
裡 is reported as a later alternative form of 裏. It is a variant relation, not evidence that 裡 is a standardized simplified form.
